title: ConflictRecord
description: What one patch submitted and the Hub did not write, kept so nothing is lost (D18, D24). There is one record per Mutation and its id is that Mutation's mutation_id, so a resend never makes a second one. The Hub makes it for every key a conflict result names in conflicted_fields and for every key of a patch refused as rejected{deleted}, and reports its id in conflict_record_ids; a suggestion.accept refused that way makes none, as the Suggestion keeps the intent. A record is open while it carries set; resolving it (conflict.resolve, from any device) removes set and writes resolved, and exactly one of the two is present. A client treats a record as open exactly when set is present. Another way of closing a record is added as a member inside resolved (resolved.how, say), never as a third state without either, so an older client still tells open from closed (D20). The Hub writes every member and syncs the record as a changes row of entity conflict_record. Open, as the Hub sends it: clients ignore members they do not know.

id.description: The mutation_id of the patch whose values this record keeps.

set.description: The changes the patch submitted for the keys that were not written, keyed and shaped as in its set. Present while the record is open.

resolved.description: When and by which conflict.resolve Mutation the record was resolved. Present once it is. A later Hub says more about how it was closed with members of its own here.

submitted_change.description: A set entry as the patch sent it (mutation change), but open.
